fix(auth): deny model access for teamless keys with all-team-models

## Relevant issues

Related to #30737 and PR #29746

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] I have requested a Greptile review by commenting `@greptileai` and received a **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

To reproduce the bug and verify the fix, start a local proxy with at least one model configured and create a teamless key with `all-team-models`:

```bash
# create a teamless key with all-team-models
curl -s http://localhost:4000/key/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"models": ["all-team-models"]}' | jq .

# before fix: this succeeds (bug) - the key can call any model despite having no team
# after fix: this returns 403 key_model_access_denied
curl -s http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GENERATED_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "gpt-4o", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}]}'
```

## Type

Bug Fix

## Changes

PR #29746 fixed `get_key_models` so that a key with `all-team-models` but no `team_id` returns an empty model list. However, two call-path functions still unconditionally skip key-level model checks when `all-team-models` is present, without checking whether the key actually belongs to a team:

1. `_enforce_key_and_fallback_model_access` (the main auth entry point for `/chat/completions` etc.) had `elif "all-team-models" in valid_token.models: pass` - skipping the model check entirely regardless of team membership

2. `can_key_call_resolved_model` (used by realtime endpoints and post-resolution checks) set `skip_key_model_check = True` whenever `all-team-models` was present, again without a team_id guard

Both now require `valid_token.team_id is not None` to skip the check. Teamless keys fall through to `can_key_call_model`, which via `_resolve_key_models_for_auth_check` correctly treats the unresolvable sentinel as a non-matching string and denies access

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/68804be8677b4a0c9033e7c2663281bc
Requested by: @mateo-berri

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Tightens proxy authorization on a sensitive path; behavior change only for teamless keys that incorrectly had `all-team-models`, which should now get 403 instead of unrestricted access.
> 
> **Overview**
> Closes an auth bypass where **virtual keys with `all-team-models` but no `team_id`** could call any model because two paths skipped key-level checks whenever that sentinel appeared.
> 
> **`can_key_call_resolved_model`** and **`_enforce_key_and_fallback_model_access`** now only skip those checks when **`valid_token.team_id is not None`**. Teamless keys run **`can_key_call_model`**, which denies access via the unresolved sentinel. Tests assert **`key_model_access_denied`** for teamless `all-team-models` on both paths.
>

answer.overlooked_assumption: The agent assumed that adding a team_id check to skip conditions would deny teamless keys, but overlooked that UserAPIKeyAuth objects default team_id to None even when a team exists, requiring explicit team_id assignment in the test fixture.
answer.why_it_breaks: The test creates a UserAPIKeyAuth without explicitly setting team_id, so it defaults to None. The production code now checks `valid_token.team_id is not None` before skipping model checks. However, in production, keys created with models=['all-team-models'] may have had team_id implicitly set or handled differently during key generation, meaning they would pass the team_id check and skip model validation. The test fixture doesn't match the production scenario where these keys were working before, causing the fix to break legitimate teamless keys that were intentionally created with all-team-models to grant broad access.

evidence.quote: Both now require `valid_token.team_id is not None` to skip the check. Teamless keys fall through to `can_key_call_model`, which via `_resolve_key_models_for_auth_check` correctly treats the unresolvable sentinel as a non-matching string and denies access
